title: COINTELPRO: The FBI's Own Files
summary: FBI Counter Intelligence Program, authorized by Hoover in 1956. Declassified files show warrantless wiretapping, surreptitious entry, mail opening, paid informants, fabricated correspondence and forged documents against civil-rights, antiwar and other groups — including the 1964 anonymous letter urging MLK to kill himself. Exposed by the 1971 Media, PA office burglary; terminated April 1971. The FBI's own Vault summary concedes it was 'rightfully criticized... for abridging first amendment rights.'
tldr: The FBI Vault's COINTELPRO index lists the program's targets: White Hate Groups, New Left, Puerto Rican Groups, Black Extremist, Hoodwink, Cuba, Socialist Workers Party, and Espionage programs — the domestic surveillance and disruption operations the Church Committee later exposed.
ai_summary:
AI review of the FBI Vault COINTELPRO index page, read in full:
- The Vault organizes the released COINTELPRO files under: White Hate Groups, New Left, Puerto Rican Groups, Black Extremist, Hoodwink, Cuba, Socialist Workers Party, and Espionage Programs.
- These are the FBI's own released files on its 1956-1971 Counter Intelligence Program — covert operations to surveil, infiltrate and disrupt domestic political groups.
- Context from the Church Committee record: COINTELPRO was 'covert action designed to disrupt and discredit' targets including the SCLC, the anti-Vietnam War movement and MLK.
- Note: this index page lists the file groupings; the underlying case files are the multi-thousand-page releases. Record summary verified consistent.
